strengths: Addresses an important interpretability problem: successful counterfactual behavior need not establish that an intervention uses the model’s native computational mechanism.

The distinction between harmless distribution shifts, hidden-pathway activation, and context-dependent dormant effects provides useful conceptual guidance. The explicit small-network constructions make these concerns concrete.

Combines observations from several intervention approaches with a constructive mitigation. In the synthetic experiment, CL regularization reduces reported feature-space divergence from 0.043 to 0.024 while approximately preserving intervention accuracy.
Includes hyperparameter explorations and explicitly acknowledges that the proposed mitigation is preliminary and does not distinguish harmless from pernicious divergence.
weaknesses: The experiments do not establish the central mitigation claim. Lower distributional distance and higher held-out intervention accuracy do not demonstrate reduced hidden-pathway recruitment or more faithful mechanism recovery. The CL method is not evaluated against the paper’s constructed pernicious cases, and its effectiveness is tested only on one simple synthetic task.

The synthetic-data specification is mathematically invalid as written. Equation 17 gives a covariance matrix with diagonal entries 0.1² and off-diagonal entries 0.2, yielding eigenvalues 0.21 and -0.19. This cannot define the stated Gaussian distribution; correcting it and clarifying the actual implementation are necessary to assess the experiments.

The theoretical treatment needs greater precision. Equation 4 does not hold complementary coordinates fixed, so it requires the entire downstream output to depend only on the selected subspace’s signs. Additionally, covariance alone does not imply that swapped coordinate combinations lie outside distributional support, as asserted in Section 4.1. Distributional displacement, low probability, and being outside support require clearer separation.

CL regression toward conditional mean representations is not generally manifold preserving: a mean can lie in a low-density region or outside a nonconvex support. Nor does matching learned causal subspaces control harmful changes in other directions. No sufficient conditions or direct evidence connect this objective to the claimed reduction of pernicious divergence.

The method’s incremental contribution is insufficiently isolated. Relative to Grant (2025), the principal changes are averaging latent targets and restricting the loss to causal subspaces, but there is no direct comparison with the original objective or factorial ablation separating these changes. Simple full-space prototype matching and projection baselines would also help establish value.

The real-model evidence demonstrates distribution differences rather than interpretability failures. In particular, SAE reconstruction error is not itself an evaluation of a targeted causal feature intervention. The limited settings and absence of corresponding mechanism-faithfulness measurements weaken the broader practical claims.

Reproducibility and uncertainty reporting are incomplete. The synthetic sample count, number of repeated runs, and meaning of error bars are unspecified; the appendix inconsistently describes input dimensionality and optimizer choice. The held-out partition protocol should also explicitly state whether any held-out representations contribute to CL target construction.

strengths: Addresses an important mechanistic interpretability question: successful behavioral interventions need not identify the mechanisms used on natural inputs.
Usefully distinguishes harmless distributional changes from interventions that recruit otherwise inactive pathways. The explicit circuit constructions make the concern concrete.

Provides observations across three intervention families and promising synthetic results: the adapted CL loss reduces reported divergence while largely preserving intervention accuracy, with additional hyperparameter exploration.
weaknesses: The main mitigation claim is not directly evaluated. Section 5 measures distributional distance and intervention accuracy, but does not demonstrate reduced hidden-pathway recruitment, fewer dormant behavioral changes, or improved recovery of native mechanisms. Better OOD accuracy alone does not establish mechanistic faithfulness.

The synthetic data specification is mathematically invalid as written. Equation 17 specifies covariance diagonals of 0.1² and off-diagonals of 0.2, yielding eigenvalues 0.21 and -0.19. This cannot define a Gaussian covariance matrix. The actual sampling procedure needs clarification before the central experiments can be reproduced.

The proposed method is an incremental modification of an existing CL loss, but comparisons do not isolate its contribution. There is no direct comparison against the original loss, nor separate ablations of averaging counterfactual targets and restricting supervision to causal subspaces. Simple supervised alignment or manifold-based alternatives are also missing.

The mitigation experiments cover only a small synthetic classification setting. The language-model experiments establish representational differences but neither demonstrate pernicious effects nor test the proposed remedy. Consequently, practical effectiveness on the models motivating the paper remains unsupported.

The theoretical treatment needs greater precision. Equation 4 does not hold other subspaces fixed, making its condition stronger than the intended sign-invariance property. Section 4.2.1's statement that the decision flips only through an off-manifold circuit overgeneralizes its own example: case 2 activates a naturally used unit. Section 4.2.2 also relies on an unspecified tie-breaking convention between classes A and B.

Closeness to averaged counterfactual representations does not generally ensure membership in the natural support or preservation of native pathways. Class means and convex interpolations can lie outside a nonconvex manifold, and restricting the loss to learned causal subspaces leaves potentially relevant joint dependencies unconstrained.

Evaluation and reproducibility details are incomplete or inconsistent: sample counts and repeated-run statistics for the synthetic experiments are insufficiently specified; the MLP input dimension is described as both 66 and 18; and Appendix A.1.2 describes a p=2 Sinkhorn computation while Equation 12 gives an unsquared-distance transport objective. The SAE experiment measures reconstruction shift rather than a targeted causal feature intervention, further limiting the interpretation of the empirical survey.

strengths: The paper addresses an important mechanistic-interpretability question: successful interventions may recruit computations that differ from the model’s natural mechanisms. Distinguishing behavioral success from mechanistic faithfulness is valuable.

The distinction between harmless divergence, hidden-pathway activation, and context-dependent dormant effects provides a useful conceptual framework. The constructed examples make these concerns concrete.

The adapted counterfactual latent loss shows promising preliminary results: reported feature-space divergence decreases from 0.043 to 0.024 with similar intervention accuracy. The appendix explores sensitivity to learning rate, subspace size, and nuisance dimensionality.
weaknesses: The experiments do not establish the central connection between divergence and misleading mechanistic conclusions in realistic models. Section 3 measures distributional differences, while harmful effects are demonstrated in constructed circuits and mitigation is evaluated on one synthetic task. No experiment directly shows that the proposed loss reduces hidden-pathway recruitment or dormant behavioral changes.

The synthetic-data specification is mathematically invalid as written. Equation 17 gives a covariance matrix with diagonal entries 0.1² and off-diagonal entries 0.2, yielding a negative eigenvalue of −0.19. The actual sampling procedure must be clarified before the results can be reproduced. Appendix A.2 also inconsistently specifies input dimensions of 66 versus 18 and describes optimization using both SGD and Adam.

The theoretical treatment contains overstatements and missing assumptions. In Section 4.2.1, only the first patched example activates the hidden unit; the second changes class through an existing pathway, contrary to the subsequent blanket claim that the decision changes only through the off-manifold circuit. Convex-hull and local-PCA projections are not generally equivalent. Section 4.2.2 also relies on an unspecified tie-breaking rule because the A and B logits are both 0.25.

The proposed loss is an incremental modification of Grant (2025), but the evaluation lacks comparisons against the original loss and ablations isolating averaging from causal-subspace restriction. Simple prototype-matching or manifold-projection baselines are also absent. Consequently, the benefit of the specific methodological contribution is unclear.

Reduced distance to a class-conditional mean does not establish manifold membership or mechanistic faithfulness: means can lie outside a nonconvex natural support, and constraining selected subspaces does not constrain the complete representation. The paper acknowledges some limitations but provides neither guarantees nor direct measurements connecting this surrogate to pernicious divergence.

The empirical divergence evidence needs stronger controls and interpretation. The SAE experiment measures reconstruction rather than a targeted feature intervention. Distributional distance can also reflect changed class frequencies or density within natural support, rather than off-support activation. These measurements alone therefore do not substantiate the broader mechanistic concern.

Reproducibility and statistical reporting are incomplete: synthetic sample counts, numbers of independent runs, error-bar definitions, and precise counterfactual-reference construction under the OOD split are not adequately specified. Appendix results also show configuration-dependent benefits, including degradations. Together with the technical issues and missing comparisons, this leaves the paper below the acceptance threshold despite its worthwhile motivation.

strengths: Addresses an important mechanistic interpretability question: successful interventions may produce the expected behavior through mechanisms absent from natural execution.

The distinction between behavioral harmlessness and faithfulness to internal computations is useful and appropriately tied to the specific mechanistic claim. The constructed examples illustrate hidden pathways and context-dependent effects.

Provides evidence of representational shifts across three method families. Applying the existing counterfactual latent loss to Boundless DAS reduces measured divergence while approximately preserving intervention accuracy; synthetic experiments include multiple seeds and hyperparameter explorations.
weaknesses: The synthetic data specification is mathematically invalid. Equation 18 gives a covariance matrix with diagonal entries 0.1² and off-diagonal entries 0.2, yielding eigenvalues 0.21 and −0.19. This cannot define the stated Gaussian distribution. Because these experiments provide the principal evidence for the modified loss and OOD benefits, the actual generation procedure needs clarification and verification.

The central practical claim remains insufficiently tested: reduced representational distance is not shown to reduce hidden-pathway activation or improve mechanistic faithfulness in a realistic model. The LLM experiment measures divergence and accuracy, while pernicious effects are demonstrated only in constructed examples. The paper acknowledges the absence of a guarantee, but still interprets distance reduction as risk reduction without directly establishing that relationship.

Novelty and comparative evidence are limited. The original CL objective comes from Grant (2025), and the new subspace-specific variant is evaluated only on a small synthetic setting. Comparisons against manifold projection, other regularizers, and controls receiving equivalent counterfactual representation supervision are missing, making it difficult to isolate the proposed modification’s contribution.

Several theoretical statements exceed their formal support. Appendix A.2 characterizes patch-closed sets as Cartesian products; the hyperrectangle conclusion requires convexity, omitted from the broader claim in Section 3.1. Existence of an off-support patch also does not establish its prevalence under realistic sampling. In Section 4.2.1, only the first patched case activates the hidden unit, although the text says the decision is crossed 'only' through an off-manifold circuit.

The empirical notion of divergence is not adequately connected to the support-based definition. Distributional distance can increase while representations remain on-support, and averaging natural counterfactual vectors need not preserve a nonconvex manifold. SAE reconstruction error is also not equivalent to evaluating targeted SAE feature interventions. Additionally, the reported p=2 Sinkhorn computation does not match the unsquared transport objective written in Equation 13.

Reproducibility and evaluation details are incomplete. The repository footnote supplies no link, important LLM settings are delegated to an external notebook, and the OOD description does not clearly specify how alignments and separately trained classifiers are combined at evaluation. The pooled regression across training objectives supports an association, but does not disentangle divergence from training-method effects.

strengths: The paper addresses an important interpretability question: successful intervention behavior need not establish that an intervention recruits the model’s natural mechanism. The distinction between behavioral validity and mechanistic validity is useful.

The constructed examples illustrate how interventions can activate otherwise inactive pathways and introduce context-dependent effects. The paper appropriately acknowledges that harmfulness depends on the claim being tested.

The experiments provide preliminary positive evidence: CL regularization reduces measured divergence while approximately preserving Boundless DAS accuracy, and the synthetic experiments report improved transfer performance, multiple seeds, and hyperparameter explorations.
weaknesses: The central mitigation claim lacks direct validation. The experiments measure distributional distance and intervention accuracy, but do not establish that CL reduces hidden-pathway activation, dormant behavioral changes, or incorrect mechanistic conclusions in trained models. Lower divergence is not itself evidence of greater mechanistic faithfulness, particularly given the paper’s own distinction between harmless and pernicious divergence.

The synthetic data specification contains a substantial technical error. Equation (18) gives a Gaussian covariance matrix with diagonal entries 0.1² and off-diagonal entries 0.2; its eigenvalues are 0.21 and −0.19, so it is not a valid covariance matrix. This may be a reporting mistake, but the actual sampling procedure must be established before the main synthetic results can be reliably interpreted or reproduced.

The theoretical claims exceed the results in places. Section 3.1 excludes every shape except axis-aligned hyperrectangles, whereas Appendix A.2 characterizes arbitrary Cartesian products; the hyperrectangle conclusion requires convexity. Existence of an off-support pair also does not establish a finite-sample guarantee or prevalence without sampling assumptions. Additionally, the constructive proof reverses the source and target arguments in its recursive patching step, so the stated coordinate-preservation invariant does not follow as written.

Distributional discrepancy, leaving the support, and leaving a manifold are insufficiently distinguished. EMD can increase through density changes entirely within the natural support. Conversely, nondegenerate Gaussian class distributions have full support, which makes the strict off-support definition in Section 4.2 unsuitable for the intended synthetic interpretation. The SAE experiment measures reconstruction discrepancy without an explicit feature intervention, further limiting what it establishes about causal intervention methods.

The proposed remedy needs stronger controls and clearer positioning. The original CL objective is explicitly borrowed from Grant (2025), while the new causal-subspace variant is evaluated only on a small synthetic grid. CL also receives counterfactual representation targets beyond the behavioral labels used by DAS. Comparisons against matched-supervision representation regression, simple projection or regularization baselines, and the original full-space CL objective are needed to isolate the contribution of the modification.

The OOD evaluation does not convincingly connect transfer gains to the proposed failure mechanism. It uses hand-designed input features and separately trained small classifiers rather than learned internal representations in realistic models. The pooled regression across training methods, seeds, and partitions establishes association but does not isolate divergence from training-method effects. The paper does not demonstrate that the observed transfer errors arise from the hidden pathways or dormant changes analyzed theoretically.

The proposed geometric safeguards have important unresolved limitations. A class-conditional average or convex-hull projection need not lie on the natural support or preserve the class. Indeed, in Section 4.2.1, the class-A midpoint [0.5, 0.5, 1, 0] is classified as B. The same section claims that the decision flips only through the hidden circuit, although its second patched example activates the first, naturally used unit instead. These qualifications matter for the conclusions drawn from the examples.

Reproducibility is incomplete: the repository footnote contains no link, the Boundless DAS setup largely delegates details to an external tutorial, synthetic sample counts are unspecified, and optimization is described inconsistently as both SGD and Adam. Checkpoint selection also differs between DAS and CL, without a sufficiently explicit validation protocol. Together with the technical and evaluation gaps, these issues place the submission below the acceptance threshold.

strengths: Addresses an important issue in mechanistic interpretability: successful behavioral interventions need not identify the mechanisms used on natural inputs.
The distinction between harmless and pernicious divergence is useful, especially the recognition that harmlessness depends on the specific mechanistic claim and evaluation context.
Provides evidence of representational divergence across three method families, supported by several complementary distance measures rather than PCA visualizations alone.

The CL experiments show promising reductions in divergence while preserving intervention accuracy. Synthetic experiments include five seeds and sensitivity analyses over learning rates and nuisance dimensions.
weaknesses: The central mitigation claim remains insufficiently validated. The LLM experiment measures divergence and intervention accuracy, but does not establish that CL reduces hidden-pathway recruitment or incorrect mechanistic conclusions. The synthetic transfer results likewise do not directly measure recovery of the true mechanism.

The synthetic data specification is mathematically invalid as written. Equation 18 gives diagonal covariance entries of 0.1² and off-diagonal entries of 0.2, yielding a negative eigenvalue. Clarifying the actual sampling implementation is necessary to assess and reproduce the principal generalization experiments.

The theoretical presentation overstates its scope. Appendix A.2 characterizes patch-closed sets as Cartesian products; the hyperrectangle conclusion requires convexity, which the broader statement in Section 3.1 omits. The proof also reverses the source/target arguments in its inductive construction. Existence of an off-support pair alone does not establish how frequently practical sampling encounters divergence.

The mitigation evaluation lacks important controls. CL receives additional counterfactual representation supervision, whereas behavioral DAS does not. Comparisons with supervised representation matching, manifold projection, and simpler regularizers are needed to isolate the benefit of the proposed subspace loss. Averaging natural representations also need not produce an on-manifold target.

Distributional discrepancy is not equivalent to the paper's formal definition of off-support divergence. EMD can increase through changes in density within the same support, and SAE reconstruction evaluates reconstruction error rather than a targeted causal feature intervention. These distinctions limit the conclusions supported by the empirical survey.

Novelty and reproducibility remain limited: the principal CL loss is inherited from Grant (2025), related interpretability illusions are already acknowledged, and the new loss is evaluated only in a small synthetic setting. Appendix A.4 delegates substantial LLM setup details to an external tutorial, while the OOD protocol does not clearly specify which classifier is used when transferring alignments between separately trained models.
